newsitem.title: RUSSIA: YELTSIN "HAS A COLD" BUT KEEPS UP NATO PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: YELTSIN "HAS A COLD" BUT KEEPS UP NATO PRESSURE.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin went down with a heavy cold on Monday but struggled through a meeting of top officials to send a tough message to the West over NATO.

Yeltsin, keen to present a vigorous image now he is back at work after almost six months off with heart problems, ordered the assembled ministers to prepare various possible responses to NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

His spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said the 65-year-old Kremlin leader had a high temperature since the morning and had cancelled several meetings planned for coming days but that the illness had no relation to Yeltsin's recent heart bypass surgery.

"Unfortunately I think the wave of flu that is going round Moscow at the moment has not passed the president's family by. Unfortunately in the president's family many people have either been ill or are now ill with flu or colds," Yastrzhembsky said.
In Sofia, Bulgarian radio reported that Bulgarian leader Petar Stoyanov had postponed a scheduled meeting to Moscow set for Wednesday because of Yeltsin's cold.
"Given the impossibility of meeting President Yeltsin, President-Elect Petar Stoyanov has postponed his working visit to Russia," his press centre was quoted as saying.
The Kremlin came under fire from political opponents last year for explaining Yeltsin's sudden disappearance just before a presidential election in June as a simple cold.
The surgeon who led Yeltsin's subsequent heart surgery said he thought the president had had a heart attack, his third.
Kremlin officials have since pledged more openness about Yeltsin's health and issued regular reports in the run-up to a quintuple bypass operation he underwent on November 5.
Yastrzhembsky said later that Yeltsin, who returned to work two weeks ago, had left the Kremlin for a residence west of Moscow and was set to recover by the end of the week.
The head of the Kremlin medical centre Sergei Mironov has visited him but a special council of doctors has not been convened, Yastrzhembsky told Itar-Tass news agency.

He said Yeltsin had gone through with Monday's hitherto unannounced meeting despite his illness because of the importance he attached to NATO-Russian relations. The spokesman said it would be the number one international issue this year.
Moscow is fiercely opposed to the Western defence alliance's plans this year to invite some former East Bloc countries to join, saying NATO expansion would threaten Russian security.
Yastrzhembsky said a weekend meeting between Yeltsin and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl had made little progress in overcoming the impasse.

Monday's meeting between Yeltsin, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais and security chiefs confirmed Moscow's opposition to the NATO expansion plans.

"A plan of action will be worked out on Russia's position, its negative position. Consequently, action plans can be worked out for various circumstances," said Yastrzhembsky, who declined to give details of what might be involved.
Yeltsin later held separate talks with Chernomyrdin "despite a heavy cold and temperature of 37.5 degrees Celsius (99.5 Fahrenheit) in the morning", the spokesman said.
"In this connection a number of meetings scheduled for the coming days have been postponed," he said, but added that preparations for future meetings were going ahead "full swing".

Apart from the Bulgarian visit, these included a summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), scheduled for January 17 in Moscow and a meeting with French President Jacques Chirac on February 2 near Moscow.
Yeltsin is also due to travel to the Hague on February 4 to meet the European Union president, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin had discussed the economy and in particular the payment of pensions which have been withheld due to a tax collection crisis.
Chernomyrdin, who would step in if Yeltsin was incapacitated, planned to take a short break near Moscow in the middle of this week, his spokesman told Tass.
